title: Role and Impact of Mass Media
summary: A modern democratic government has a Legislature (State Assemblies and Parliament, which frame laws), an Executive (Governor, Chief Minister, President, Prime Minister and ministers, who run the state and country) and a Judiciary (Supreme Court, High Courts and other courts, which see that laws and the Constitution are followed). The main role of mass media is to act as a bridge between the people and the government, so media is called the fourth institution (fourth pillar) of democracy. Example: the media convey and explain the effect of a decision on petrol and diesel prices and inform farmers about a new high-yielding variety. The media use print, radio, television, traditional media and the internet. The central government's media agencies work under the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (information and broadcasting departments); state governments have their own agencies.
## Functions and responsibilities of the media

Mass media are a source of information; they can help bring change in attitudes and habits (HIV/AIDS myths, polio drops on polio day) and change for the better in development (media can also demonstrate skills, such as cooking with modern equipment); they have made the world smaller and closer ('global village') through live television and the internet; and they promote distribution of goods through advertising of products and services, helping industry and consumers.

Media have great power, so they need a code of ethics. For lawyers and doctors there are clear codes; for mass media there are only a few guidelines and no strict code. The Press Council of India issues guidelines on media ethics. Codes: accuracy (verify facts, give the accused a chance to give a version); confidentiality of information from sources; protection of sources (never reveal the source); right to privacy (do not write about the private life of ordinary citizens); no incitement to violence; no vulgarity or obscenity; no communal writing (India is secular; media reports have triggered riots).

Positive: provide news and information, educate, help democracy function (inform about policies and carry people's feelings to government), entertain, act as an agent of change in development, bring the world closer, promote trade and industry through advertisements, help political and democratic processes and bring positive social change. Negative: adversely affect traditional culture; entertainment dominates and reduces the aim to inform and educate; promote violence (harmful to children); promote desire to buy products that may not be essential.

objective: Fill in the blanks: Media is considered the ______ institution of democracy; the government is run by ______.
State true or false: (i) Mass media have a strict code of conduct like doctors. (ii) Media can change people's attitudes and habits.
Name any two ethical codes for media persons.
Accuracy, confidentiality, protection of sources, right to privacy (any two).
Match: (i) Legislature (ii) Executive (iii) Judiciary with (a) Supreme Court (b) Parliament (c) Prime Minister.
vsa: The whole world is shrinking and becoming like a village because media bring people closer through live events and the internet.
Name the three institutions of a modern democratic government.
How do mass media promote distribution of goods?
Through advertising, media inform people about products, services and prices.
Why is 'protection of sources' an ethical code?
Revealing a confidential source may harm that person, so media must never disclose the source.
sa: Explain the role of mass media in society.

Media inform and educate the people, change attitudes and habits (polio, HIV/AIDS), act as a bridge between government and public, bring the world closer, support trade through advertising and entertain.
Elucidate any three ethical principles that media professionals should follow.

Accuracy: verify facts before publishing. Right to privacy: do not report on the private life of ordinary citizens. No incitement to violence or communal writing: do not provoke violence or communal problems.
List any three positive and any three negative effects of media.
Positive: informs and educates, helps democracy, promotes trade. Negative: harms traditional culture, promotes violence, creates desire for non-essential products.
la: Explain the relationship between mass media and democracy.

Legislature, Executive and Judiciary run government; media are the bridge, informing people about government decisions and bringing public reactions to the government, hence the fourth institution; government agencies under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting use media for policies.
What are media ethics? List the ethical codes to be practised by media persons.

Media ethics are guidelines on right and wrong for media persons because they are powerful. Codes: accuracy, confidentiality, protection of sources, right to privacy, no incitement to violence, no vulgarity or obscenity and no communal writing; the Press Council of India issues guidelines.
